steps.caption: Most of Spain has a Mediterranean climate. It has three variations: typical Mediterranean, inland Mediterranean and dry Mediterranean.
All three variations have low total annual precipitation, less than 600 l/m² per year, and summer drought: hot, dry summers with little precipitation.
Typical Mediterranean, for example in Huelva: mild winters, hot summers and scarce, irregular precipitation.
Inland Mediterranean, for example in Valladolid: very cold winters, hot summers and scarce, irregular precipitation.
Dry Mediterranean, for example in Almería: high temperatures all year round and very scarce precipitation.
Plants grow in different places depending on the climate. The Mediterranean forest includes holm oaks, cork oaks and pines. Fan palms and esparto grass grow in the driest areas.
